title: Availability vs consistency — CAP and PACELC
summary: What CAP really says, why the real choice under a partition is C vs A, how PACELC adds the latency trade-off when there is no partition, and reading nines of availability.
note:
1. CAP
   • A distributed system faces partitions (P) — not optional
   • During a partition you pick Consistency OR Availability
   • CP = reject/stall to stay correct · AP = answer with maybe-stale data
2. PACELC
   • If Partition → C vs A · Else (normal) → Latency vs Consistency
   • Even with no partition, strong consistency costs round-trips
3. Availability nines
   • 99.9% ≈ 8.7h/yr down · 99.99% ≈ 52min · 99.999% ≈ 5min
✎ In my words: ______________________________________________

recall.q: During a network partition, what is the real CAP choice?
recall.a: Consistency vs availability: refuse/stall to stay correct (CP), or answer with possibly stale data (AP).

recall.q: What does the 'ELC' in PACELC add?
recall.a: Even with no partition (Else), you trade Latency against Consistency.

recall.q: Rough downtime for 99.99% availability per year?

shot.title: CAP / PACELC quick read
shot.body:
| system | partition choice | notes |
|---|---|---|
| CP store (e.g. ZooKeeper/HBase) | consistency | may reject writes when split |
| AP store (e.g. Dynamo/Cassandra) | availability | serves stale, reconciles later |
| PACELC | P→C/A, E→L/C | captures the normal-case latency cost |

sections.title: What CAP actually says
sections.body:
✍️ CAP: among **Consistency**, **Availability**, **Partition tolerance**, you can guarantee only two. In a real network partitions happen, so **P is not optional** — the design decision is C vs A *during a partition*.
✍️ **CP:** when nodes can't talk, refuse or stall writes/reads to never return wrong data. **AP:** keep answering using local data that might be stale, reconcile later.

sections.title: PACELC — the part CAP leaves out
sections.body:
✍️ PACELC: *if* **P**artition, choose **A** vs **C**; *else* (**E**, the common case) choose **L**atency vs **C**onsistency.
✍️ It names the everyday cost CAP ignores: strong consistency needs extra coordination round-trips, which adds latency even when nothing is broken.

sections.title: Strong vs eventual consistency
sections.body:
✍️ **Strong:** a read always sees the latest committed write (needs a leader/quorum). **Eventual:** replicas converge over time; a read may lag.
- Pick eventual for feeds, counters, caches; pick strong for money, inventory, unique constraints.

sections.title: Reading availability nines
sections.body:
✍️ Availability is uptime fraction. 99.9% ("three nines") ≈ 8.7 hours down/year; 99.99% ≈ 52 min; 99.999% ≈ 5 min. Each extra nine is roughly 10× less downtime and much more cost.
```java
// Eventual consistency in code: tolerate a stale read, confirm on the critical path
long views = cache.getOrDefault(postId, 0L); // may lag
if (isCheckout) views = db.readAuthoritative(postId); // pay for strong read only when it matters
```
